subject: Data residency mapping & timed-deletion attestation — sample artifacts needed
messages:
From: Alice Liu <alice.liu@bigbank.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference>
Cc: BigBank Security <security@bigbank.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:14:22 -0700
Subject: Request: residency mapping + deletion attestation (SOC2 evidence)

Hi David,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As part of our SOC2 readiness review we need to validate two specific controls around tenant data lifecycle:

1) A residency map showing where tenant data is stored (region/geozone) and which storage class each tenant uses.
2) Evidence of timed deletion (TTL) for a representative sample of tenants, including deletion timestamps and proof (hash lists or log entries).

Acceptance criteria from our auditors: per-tenant residency mapping (CSV or spreadsheet), a sampling of deletion events with timestamps and corresponding object IDs/hashes, and a short note describing the deletion workflow and where audit logs are stored.

Can you provide a scoped artifact set for a 10-tenant sample by EOD Friday? If not possible, let us know the earliest date you can deliver and any constraints (e.g., manual redaction, data retention holds).

I attached a template that shows the auditor's preferred columns (tenant_id, region, storage_class, created_at, deleted_at, object_hash).

Regards,
Alice Liu
Information Security — BigBank

Attachment: evidence-request-template.xlsx (XLSX, 18 KB)
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference>
To: Alice Liu <alice.liu@bigbank.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 10:02:11 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: residency mapping + deletion attestation (SOC2 evidence)

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear scope. We'll take this on. Quick notes / clarifying Qs before we pull artifacts:

- Are auditors ok with a hashed tenant_id column rather than raw tenant IDs? We can provide salted hashes to protect PII while still proving per-tenant provenance.
- For deletion proof, do you need per-object cryptographic hashes or is a per-tenant deletion manifest + audit-log entries sufficient? Auditors typically accept a manifest + corresponding log entries showing when the deletion job ran and which object IDs were removed.

Action plan (targeting your Friday EOD):
- Monica: produce residency_map CSV (tenant -> primary geozone + storage class + retention TTL).
- Rachel: extract deletion samples (10 tenants) and render deletion manifests + audit log snippets; include object hashes where feasible.
- I'll assemble a short runbook summary describing the TTL enforcement and safe-hold/exception process.

If there are any tenants with active legal holds we should exclude them — please let us know if BigBank wants specific tenants included/excluded.

I'll loop back with an ETA for the first drop by noon Thursday.

Thanks,
David Kim
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: (none)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference>, Alice Liu <alice.liu@bigbank.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 12:30:04 -07:00
Subject: Residency map (preliminary)

Hi all — attaching the preliminary residency map for your 10-tenant sample. Columns follow the auditor template: tenant_hash, primary_region, storage_class, created_at, configured_ttl_days.

Notes:
- We hashed tenant_id with a per-request salt (not shared) to avoid exposing clear tenant identifiers in an external workflow. If auditors require original tenant_ids we can provide them under an NDA or through an encrypted transfer.
- Some tenants have multi-region replication and are marked as PRIMARY_REGION = us-west-2 with REPLICAS = eu-west-1 in the comments column.
- Storage_class uses our internal tags (hot/warm/archival).

Attachment: residency-map.csv (CSV, 14 KB)

On the deletion sample: we can pull manifests, but object-level hashes require a secondary extraction run (we store object hashes in a separate audit bucket). That will add ~2 hours to Rachel's work.

Monica Patel
Data Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Liu <alice.liu@bigbank.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference>
Cc: BigBank Security <security@bigbank.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 14:20:07 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency map (preliminary)

Thanks Monica — the residency map looks good at a glance. A few follow-ups from the auditors:

- Hashing: salted hashes are fine for initial review; auditors will eventually want a cross-walk for a handful of tenants under secure transfer.
- Deletion proof: preference is per-object hash + deletion timestamp for the sampled objects. If that adds a few hours, that's OK — please include the estimation.
- Workflow: we need a short paragraph describing the TTL enforcement (what service performs deletion, typical job cadence, how retries/exceptions are handled) plus the location of the immutable audit logs and their retention window.

Can you confirm ETA for the deletion manifest + object hashes and push artifacts to the secure drop? Also, please call out any known TTL exemptions (escrows, legal holds) in the note column of the CSV.

Best,
Alice
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>
To: Alice Liu <alice.liu@bigbank.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 16:03:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency mapping & timed-deletion attestation — sample artifacts needed

Thanks — putting the sample set together now. Deliverables attached:

- deletion-samples-20260601.zip: per-tenant deletion manifests (10 tenants) including object IDs and deletion timestamps. Each manifest contains an object_id and deleted_at column.
- audit-log-sample-202605.csv: the corresponding audit log entries from the deletion service for those runs.

Notes on hashes and provenance:
- We extracted object-level SHA256 hashes for the sample and included them in the ZIP under per-tenant manifests (folder: object_hashes/). Generating those hashes required a read of the archival audit bucket; this added ~2.5 hours to the job.
- Audit logs are retained in our immutable logging tier for 18 months; sample entries are redacted for any PII. Full unredacted logs can be made available under an encrypted transfer if the auditor requests them.
- TTL enforcement: our scheduled deletion job runs hourly, keyed by tenant TTL metadata. Retries: failed deletes go into a retry queue for 24 hours; if still failing, they create an incident and remain until manual remediation. Exceptions: registered legal holds are stored in the tenant metadata table and prevent the deletion job from queuing for that tenant.

I uploaded the artifacts to the secured SFTP drop (link below) and provided your security inbox temporary download credentials that expire in 72 hours.

Secure drop: sftp://evidence-drop.redwood.inference/BigBank/20260805 (credentials sent separately)

Attachments: deletion-samples-20260601.zip (ZIP, 2.1 MB); audit-log-sample-202605.csv (CSV, 45 KB)

Next steps: David/Rachel/Monica — if auditors want a live walkthrough we can schedule a 30-minute screen share Thursday morning.

--
Rachel Kim
Compliance Engineer, Data Lifecycle
Redwood Inference
